descriptions.text: Soul Crystal. C-Grade. Elf technology. It's like a wireless charger. Instead of electricity, it runs on the soul power of everything killed within the area. And instead of charging your iPhone, this particular gem tops off the town's Swordsmen guards each night. Some of that power is also leeching into something else. If this crystal is physically touched by living flesh, it will shatter and cease to work.

recap.text: Hundreds of Swordsmen guards stand in stasis below, a yellow aura leading to a point in the ceiling. Above, a golf-ball-sized amber soul crystal floats, tethered to Remex's chest, and Carl shuts a glass case round it. The blast goes off silently inside the case, one ray striking Remex's chest, and Carl grabs the gem, burning the skin off his fingers. It is his Doomsday Scenario now, made of the soul crystal and a Sheol Glass Reaper Case.

Carl tells Elle that soul crystals run the ghoul generators and don't take kindly to being blown up. A far-off explosion reaches him: 300 to 400 crawlers had gone to wreck the generator at a station 72. Tizquick the dwarf helps Elle's away team find the line there, where the ceiling has caved in but the circle of stairwells stands, cleared of rubble. Crawlers flock to descend without fighting, so the dead did not die in vain.

Carl finds a grape-sized, colourless gem that glitters as it moves in a hologram of goods on offer, and he takes it for a soul crystal. Soul crystals are worthless once installed as a power source, unless used as an explosive, but this gem is listed as something else. Mordecai explains that elves mine their power-source crystals from Scolopendra's lair, where the souls of certain dead people are filtered through the centipede's body.

beats.headline: A point in the ceiling
beats.text: Through the open door of the warehouse's first level, even in the dark, Carl can see the inactive Swordsmen guards: hundreds of them in silent formation, like the terracotta army, with no dots over them on his map. A yellow aura swirls round their metallic bodies, and all of it leads to a point in the ceiling. There would be a soul crystal up there somewhere. At night, Mordecai says, the guards are in stasis and invulnerable, so locking them in and blowing them up over and over is out.
beats.gist: Carl sees hundreds of dormant Swordsmen guards, their yellow auras all leading to a ceiling point.

beats.headline: The Amplifier
beats.text: In the room above the warehouse a golf-ball-sized amber jewel floats, tethered to Remex's chest by a thread of golden light, a stalk of light running down through the floor. Carl examines it: a C-grade soul crystal that charges the swordsmen each night and shatters if living flesh touches it. With Miss Quill gone, Remex says, there is no siphon tonight. The roof is the antennae, he explains, and the soul crystal stores the power: that is the Amplifier. The map puts the gem at the epicentre of the coming blast. Breaking it, Mordecai thinks, would only make it blow early. A red timer appears over it.
beats.gist: Remex's soul crystal, the Amplifier, stores the roof's power and would only blow early if broken.

beats.headline: Half of a bomb
beats.text: The explosion goes off silently inside the glass case Carl closed round the gem. Light streams from the container like a miniature, caged sun, one lance-like ray straight into Remex's chest, and the floorboards bubble and burn. The case and the gem have transformed. Carl reads Status: Explosion Imminent in the two seconds before he grabs it and pulls it into his inventory, burning the skin off his fingers. It is Carl's Doomsday Scenario now, created by combining a massively overloaded soul crystal and a Sheol Glass Reaper Case.
beats.gist: Carl burns his fingers pocketing a caged, overloaded soul crystal, now his Doomsday Scenario.

beats.headline: The ghoul generators
beats.text: The fourth floor's Blister Ghouls come out of soul crystal-powered ghoul generators, one ghoul for every non-undead mob that dies on the floor, and every mob on the floor is suffering from something that will kill it. Goddamn soul crystals, Carl thinks: they powered the swordsmen on the third floor and Miss Quill's spell, and one became the bomb still sitting in his inventory, which he has not dared take out at his sapper's table. The generators are run by soul crystals, he tells Elle, and they don't take kindly to being blown up.
beats.gist: Soul crystals power the ghoul generators, and Carl tells Elle they dislike being blown up.

beats.headline: A blast far off
beats.text: An explosion far away is still loud and powerful enough to be felt where Carl is. A team of something like 300 to 400 crawlers had set out to fight their way to the blister ghoul generator at one of the station 72s, to remove the crystal or disable the machine. I think they blew the soul crystal, Carl says; he warned them it was dangerous. He tells Imani and Elle to send a group to find the line there: if the generator blew, everything over there is dead, but the stairwells might still be open.
beats.gist: Carl hears a far-off explosion and fears the crawlers blew the soul crystal.

beats.headline: Not in vain
beats.text: Elle's away team, with the help of Tizquick the dwarf, finds the right coloured line to the exploded station 72, where plenty of other crawlers had the same idea. The ceiling has caved in, but the circle of stairwells remains, and people have cleared the rubble. Word goes out that it is a place to descend without fighting, and crawlers flock to it. The ones who died blowing the soul crystal did not, at least, die in vain.
beats.gist: Crawlers flock to station 72's cleared stairwells; the dead did not die in vain.

beats.headline: Mined from the centipede
beats.text: In a hologram of goods on offer sits a grape-sized, colourless gem that glitters as it moves. Carl takes it for a soul crystal at first. Those are without value once installed as a power source, unless used as an explosive; unused ones are supposedly rare and treasured. This one is listed as something else. Mordecai explains: the soul crystals elves use to power their things are mined from Scolopendra's lair, created when certain types of people die and their souls are filtered through the centipede's body. Memorial crystals are similar, but made by fallen gods and demigods.
beats.gist: Mordecai explains that elves mine soul crystals, made from certain dead people's filtered souls, in Scolopendra's lair.

relations.note: his capacitor leeches off the souls flowing into it
